## 8\. Exact algorithm and worst-case bit resources

The algorithm is\:

1. Read the rational input and calculate \(R\) exactly, using integer numerator–denominator arithmetic.
2. Set \(M=R^6\), \(n=R^{200}\), \(A_0=R^{100}\)\.
3. Form \(D_M\) and compute its 32nd Fourier power by exact integer convolution.
4. Form the three components (4), using rational quarter-period phase shifts.
5. Multiply the coefficients by \(nA_0\) and their Fourier frequencies by \(n\)\.
6. Output the resulting finite rational sine–cosine expansion.

There is no controller search and no evaluation of an infinite-dimensional semigroup.

### Final implementation bounds

| Resource | Bound |
|--------|--------|
| Largest Fourier coordinate frequency | \(32R^{206}\) |
| \(\\|b\\|_\infty\) | \(2R^{300}\) |
| \(\\|\nabla b\\|_\infty\) | \(10^4R^{506}\) |
| \(\\|b\\|_{W^{1,\infty}}\) | \(10^5R^{506}\) |
| Fourier term count | \(O(R^{12})\) |
| Raw rational coefficient height | \(10\cdot3^{64}R^{684}\) |
| Fourier description bit length | \(O(R^{12}\log(2R))\) |
| Deterministic bit work | \(O((B+R)^{30})\) |
| Working memory | \(O((B+R)^{20})\) |

The bit-work estimates use schoolbook integer arithmetic; faster multiplication is unnecessary. Computing the initial rational sum defining \(R\) requires polynomial bit work in \(B\)\. All subsequent integers have polynomially bounded numerical height in \(R\)\.

A single conservative common resource pair is

\[
\boxed{
C=10^{100},\qquad c=1000.
}
\]

### Certification and numerical precision

The contraction certificate is analytic and uniform; it does not need a Galerkin matrix at all.

The relevant parameter comparisons involve integer powers of \(R\), and inequalities such as

\[
R^{79}>10^{12},\qquad
R^{149}>4\cdot10^{60},\qquad R\geq9.
\]

They are decidable by exact integer arithmetic.

The fixed trigonometric inequalities used in the proof can be established symbolically, using elementary rational bounds on \(\pi\)\. No input-dependent approximation to \(\pi\), no spectral conditioning parameter, and no adjustable numerical tolerance is needed.

Thus the full construction and its resource verification remain finite-word Turing computations.

---

## 9\. Physical actuation and continuing service

The theorem establishes an algorithmic and kinematic control primitive. It does not establish an energy-efficient physical stirring mechanism.
